# Linear Algebra — heuristics

## [Linear maps](linear-maps.md)
- To define a linear map, say where a basis goes. Everything else is forced.
- To show a map is not linear, check T(0) = 0 first. Many non-examples fail there.

## [Image](linear-maps/image.md)
- To find the image of a matrix, take the span of its columns.
- Kernel lives in the domain, image lives in the codomain. Say which space you are in before computing.

## [Kernel](linear-maps/kernel.md)
- When asked if T is injective, check whether ker T = {0} first.
- To find a kernel, set T(v) = 0 and solve. The solution set is the kernel.

## [Vector spaces](vector-spaces.md)
- To show a set is a subspace, check 0 first. Most non-examples fail there.
- To show a set is not a subspace, find one pair whose sum leaves the set, or one vector whose negative leaves it.

## [Basis](vector-spaces/basis.md)
- To turn a spanning list into a basis, throw out vectors that are in the span of the earlier ones.
- To turn an independent list into a basis, keep adding vectors outside the current span.

## [Span](vector-spaces/span.md)
- To test independence, set the combination to 0 and see if the coefficients are forced to 0.
- A list with more vectors than the dimension of the space is dependent. Count first.
